SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where does the sun set? (1 mark)
   A. In the north
   B. In the east
   C. In the west
   D. In the south

2. How many cardinal points are there on a compass? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Two
   C. Six
   D. Four

3. On a map of a village, the church is to the east of the school. On the map, where is the church drawn? (1 mark)
   A. Above the school
   B. On the right of the school
   C. On the left of the school
   D. Below the school

4. Which ocean is found on the south-eastern side of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Arctic Ocean
   B. Atlantic Ocean
   C. Pacific Ocean
   D. Indian Ocean

5. What do we call describing where a county is by naming the places around it? (1 mark)
   A. Population
   B. Scale
   C. Relative location
   D. Rainfall

6. What does a map key explain? (1 mark)
   A. The name of the map maker
   B. The weather
   C. The date of the map
   D. The meaning of the colours and symbols

7. Which physical feature is best for building roads, towns and farms easily? (1 mark)
   A. A deep valley
   B. A plain
   C. A waterfall
   D. A steep mountain

8. Which valley runs from north to south through Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The Coast Valley
   B. The Tana Valley
   C. The Great Rift Valley
   D. The Kisumu Valley

9. On a physical map, what colour is often used for high mountains? (1 mark)
   A. Pink
   B. Brown
   C. Blue
   D. White

10. If there is no pavement, which side of the road should a pedestrian walk on? (1 mark)
   A. On the side where there is no light
   B. The side facing the oncoming traffic
   C. The side with traffic behind
   D. In the middle of the road

11. What is a season? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of clothing
   B. A type of crop
   C. The weather on one day
   D. A part of the year with a typical kind of weather

12. Where should you shelter during a thunderstorm? (1 mark)
   A. Under a tall tree
   B. Beside a river
   C. In an open field
   D. In a strong building

13. What does UNESCO do for important old places? (1 mark)
   A. Helps to protect them
   B. Moves them to other countries
   C. Sells them
   D. Paints them

14. Which is a very old town on the Kenyan coast with narrow streets and stone houses? (1 mark)
   A. Thimlich Ohinga
   B. Nakuru
   C. Eldoret
   D. Lamu Old Town

15. What is a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. A bank
   B. A hospital
   C. A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive
   D. A place for repairing cars

16. Which of these is a service? (1 mark)
   A. Treatment by a nurse
   B. A book
   C. A bag of maize
   D. A pair of shoes

17. Which of these is a good? (1 mark)
   A. A pair of shoes
   B. Teaching
   C. Driving a matatu
   D. Nursing

18. Which is a way of showing appreciation for others? (1 mark)
   A. Breaking their tools
   B. Ignoring their help
   C. Saying thank you
   D. Laughing at their work

19. What is population? (1 mark)
   A. The rainfall in a place
   B. The size of a place
   C. The number of animals in a place
   D. The number of people living in a place

20. Which is a reason why fewer people live in a forest reserve? (1 mark)
   A. There are too many houses
   B. It has many towns
   C. People are not allowed to settle there
   D. It has good roads

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State three road safety rules for a rainy day. (3 marks)

22. State three benefits of interdependence in a county. (3 marks)

23. Explain three ways in which a county can benefit when its officers know its size and location well. (3 marks)

24. Explain how a cultural centre is different from a museum. (3 marks)

25. State two things that a visitor can learn in a museum. (2 marks)

26. Explain why Kenya does not have summer and winter. (2 marks)

27. Name the five countries that border Kenya. (5 marks)

28. Give three things that should be on a sketch map of your county. (3 marks)

29. Describe how you would show a river, a lake and a mountain on a map with a key. (3 marks)

30. A weather chart for a week shows: Mon sunny, Tue sunny, Wed rainy, Thu cloudy, Fri rainy, Sat sunny, Sun cloudy. How many days were sunny, rainy and cloudy? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — In the west
   The sun sets in the west.

2. D — Four
   There are four cardinal points: north, east, south and west.

3. B — On the right of the school
   East is on the right when north is at the top.

4. D — Indian Ocean
   Kenya's coast is on the Indian Ocean.

5. C — Relative location
   Relative location compares a place with its neighbours.

6. D — The meaning of the colours and symbols
   The key tells what each line, colour and symbol stands for.

7. B — A plain
   Flat land is easy to build on and farm.

8. C — The Great Rift Valley
   The Great Rift Valley runs through Kenya.

9. B — Brown
   Brown shows high land such as mountains.

10. B — The side facing the oncoming traffic
   Facing traffic lets you see vehicles coming towards you.

11. D — A part of the year with a typical kind of weather
   A season is the weather that is typical over several months.

12. D — In a strong building
   Lightning can strike tall trees, so a building is safer.

13. A — Helps to protect them
   UNESCO names World Heritage Sites and helps to protect them.

14. D — Lamu Old Town
   Lamu Old Town is one of the oldest towns on the coast.

15. C — A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive
   Cultural centres show dances, homes, crafts and foods.

16. A — Treatment by a nurse
   A service is work done for someone. The others are goods.

17. A — A pair of shoes
   Goods are things we can touch and use.

18. C — Saying thank you
   Thanking people shows we value them.

19. D — The number of people living in a place
   Population is the number of people in an area.

20. C — People are not allowed to settle there
   Forest reserves are protected.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not cross flooded roads, wear bright or reflective clothes, and walk facing traffic if there is no pavement.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: People get goods and services they cannot make, people help each other in trouble, and the county develops faster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: They can plan roads and health centres to reach people. They can share resources with neighbours. They can plan journeys and services better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: A museum mainly keeps and shows objects. A cultural centre lets people see and join in living culture such as dances and crafts. Some places do both.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: How people lived long ago and which tools they used. Accept learning about animals, plants and cultures.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Kenya lies on the equator, so the temperature changes little through the year. Our seasons depend mainly on rain and on how high the land is.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the equator idea, 1 mark for rain or height.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Uganda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, South Sudan and Somalia.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each country.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: A title, a north arrow and a key. Accept sub-county names and boundaries.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wavy blue line for a river, a blue patch for a lake and a brown triangle or brown shading for a mountain, with a key that explains them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct symbol described, up to 3.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 sunny days, 2 rainy days and 2 cloudy days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct count. Check: 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 days.
